critical.finding: Finance leases are treated two different ways. The bridge deducts the existing 70,973M of finance-lease liabilities as a debt-like claim, which is correct and not double counted (see the minor finding below). But the base sales_to_capital of 0.75 is computed on cash capex minus D&A only, described as 'before finance-lease additions'. D&A is taken net of finance-lease depreciation, but the lease additions themselves are left out. The 10-K lease note (reading/10k_full.txt around line 7408, 'Right-of-use assets obtained in exchange for lease obligations: Finance leases') gives 11,633M in FY2024, 20,511M in FY2025 and 24,608M in FY2026, and the 10-Q gives 5,192M for Q1 FY2027. Adding the 56.8B of FY2024-FY2026 finance-lease additions to the 153.5B of net capex gives 119.9 / 210.3 = 0.57, not 0.78. FY2026 alone is 50.1 / 106.2 = 0.47, not 0.61. So the base 0.75 understates reinvestment by about a quarter during the growth years. The bear's 0.55, described as 'below the FY2026 low', is actually above the lease-inclusive FY2026 figure of 0.47. The fair value of 546 is only 4% above the price of 523, so the table's 'cheap' reading depends on this lever. Future lease-funded datacenter capacity is also left out of reinvestment, including the 364.6B of leases not yet commenced, while the existing leases are deducted as debt. That pairing favors the value.

critical.fix: Register the finance-lease ROU additions from the 10-K lease note (FY2024 11,633M, FY2025 20,511M, FY2026 24,608M; source pf_10k) and from the 10-Q (Q1 FY2027 5,192M; pf_10q_20261028). Recompute sales_to_capital as incremental revenue / (cash capex + finance-lease ROU additions - D&A), which gives a three-year figure of about 0.57 and FY2026 of about 0.47. Reset bear, base and bull around that basis, keeping the bear below the lease-inclusive FY2026 low. Rerun ticker-value. The alternative is to stop treating finance leases as debt and treat their payments as operating costs, but one of the two treatments must be chosen and used throughout.

The analyst's own evidenced path uses ROIC 22% base / 14% bear / 31% bull, in line with the 3-year incremental ROIC of 22.5-23.6% (prefetch/forensic.json roic.incremental_roic; redteam detail incremental_roic_3y 0.225) while capex doubled. The two parts of one base story disagree by ~17 pp of ROIC: at the path's 22% the base value today is 489$ (economics.values year 0), i.e. the stock is ~7% ABOVE base value, not 4% below. The what_must_be_true capital_efficiency lever confirms it: the price holds only if growth needs at most 1.18x the base capital (terminal ROIC >= ~33%).
